mainTopic: Leniencies about found corpses, doubts in נגעים, and checking a זב before and after he is confirmed
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of corpses found buried in a field. רבא rules on someone who found and moved two corpses one at a time and then found a third. In a second version, רבא lets him move the third one too. ריש לקיש explains that חכמים looked for any reason to keep ארץ ישראל pure, and the same idea explains why a twenty-אמה search that finds nothing ends the worry. A new משנה then teaches that a doubt about נגעים is pure at the start, but impure once the person has been declared impure. The גמרא shows that רב's פסוק, which mentions purity first, really explains רבי יהושע's view in the case of the בהרת and the white hair. Next, a משנה teaches that before a man is confirmed as a זב, we check seven outside causes of his discharge, and after that we stop checking. It adds the case of a beaten victim who got better and then died, where רבי נחמיה uses the idea of רגלים לדבר. רבי נתן learns the זב rule from ״והזב את זובו״, and רבי אליעזר's view is explained by his learning from the word את.

steps.title: Found two corpses one at a time, then a third
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that once a third corpse is found, it may not be moved to join the first two, and the first two are not brought back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone checked, found a corpse, and moved it, then checked again, found another, and moved it, and then checked a third time and found another, he does not move this third one to where he put the two. He also does not bring those two back to be with this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on a case where a person moved two found corpses one at a time and then found a third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה taught that one lone corpse may be moved, but three corpses together make a שכונת קברות, a real graveyard, which may not be moved. Once the third is found, it becomes clear this was a graveyard, so the third stays put. But the first two were moved with permission, so he does not have to bring them back.

keyTerms.meaning: he moved it, he cleared it away

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a move done with permission is not undone, even when later facts would have forbidden it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he checked and moved it, then checked and moved it,
then checked and found a third —

phrases.aramaic: לָא הַאי מְפַנֵּי לֵיהּ גַּבֵּי הָנָךְ תְּרֵי,
phrases.english: he does not move this one over to those two,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא הָנֵי תְּרֵי לְגַבַּי הַאי חַד.
phrases.english: and he does not bring those two back to this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּדַק וּפִנָּה, בָּדַק וּפִנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by applying the earlier משנה's rule about one corpse versus three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third corpse stays in place, and the first two are not returned.

steps.title: Second version: he may move the third one too
steps.stepSummary: Another report of רבא's words: since he was allowed to move the first ones, he may move the third as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבא said: Since permission was given to move them, he may move them all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of what רבא said, and this version is more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the first two moves were allowed, so the three were never found lying together as a group. That means the third is treated like a single corpse and may be moved too.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion arguing with רבא. It is a second report of what רבא himself said.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rava said:
Since permission was given to move them,
he may move them.
phrases.notes: He means all of them, including the third one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a more lenient version of רבא's ruling from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the earlier moves were allowed, the third corpse may also be moved.

steps.title: Why not treat them as a graveyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the lenient version: three corpses were found, so it should count as a שכונת קברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us treat them as a graveyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבא: three corpses were found here, so this should be a graveyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that three corpses make a שכונת קברות. It seems strange to ignore that just because they were found one at a time. Being stricter would make sense, since there may be more corpses nearby.

keyTerms.meaning: let us treat them as, let us make them
a graveyard; an area where three or more corpses are found together

phrases.english: But let us treat them as a graveyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient version in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבא, which lets him move the third corpse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three corpses were found in one area, which is the definition of a שכונת קברות, so they should not be moved.

steps.title: חכמים looked for a reason to keep ארץ ישראל pure
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that חכמים grabbed onto any reason to declare ארץ ישראל pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: They found a reason and declared ארץ ישראל pure.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge: חכמים wanted to keep the land pure, so they used any good reason to be lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the corpses were not found together at one time, there was room to say this is not a graveyard. חכמים used that opening on purpose to avoid spreading doubts of טומאה across ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: a reason, an opening, a pretext

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key to the whole section, and the גמרא uses it again in step 8.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They found a reason and declared the Land of Israel pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: עִילָּא, מָצְאוּ וְטִיהֲרוּ אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Policy principle: חכמים chose to be lenient
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three corpses should automatically make a graveyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since they were not found together, חכמים used that opening to keep ארץ ישראל pure.

steps.title: Searched twenty אמות and found nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if he searched twenty אמות around the corpses and found nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he searched twenty אמות away and found nothing, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about what happens after searching twenty אמות and finding no more corpses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that after finding a graveyard, one searches twenty אמות around it. The question is what that empty search means for the status of the area.

keyTerms.meaning: twenty cubits, the search distance around a graveyard

phrases.aramaic: בָּדַק מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וְלֹא מָצָא, מַאי?
phrases.english: If he searched twenty cubits and did not find anything, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּדַק מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וְלֹא מָצָא, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the twenty-אמה search.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of the area when a twenty-אמה search finds nothing.

steps.title: It is a graveyard, and that is all
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the place where the corpses were found is a שכונת קברות, and there is no worry beyond that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר ירמיה said in the name of רב: It is a graveyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers: the corpses found are a graveyard, and the empty search means we stop there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The found corpses keep the status of a שכונת קברות. But since nothing more turned up within twenty אמות, we do not worry about more corpses farther away.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya said that Rav said:
It is a graveyard.
phrases.notes: He means just the corpses found are the graveyard, so no need to worry about more beyond it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a שכונת קברות, limited to what was found.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we are not worried about more corpses farther away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where there are three corpses, there could easily be more beyond twenty אמות. So the גמרא wants to know why we may be lenient.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is no worry about corpses beyond the twenty-אמה search.

steps.title: Same principle: keep ארץ ישראל pure
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's principle answers again: חכמים found a reason to declare ארץ ישראל pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: They found a reason and declared ארץ ישראל pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same rule of ריש לקיש from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The empty twenty-אמה search gave חכמים an opening to say there are no more corpses. They took it so that ארץ ישראל would stay pure.
steps.whatToRemember: Both leniencies in this section, moving the third corpse and not worrying beyond twenty אמות, rest on one idea: עילא מצאו וטיהרו את ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: עִילָּא מָצְאוּ וְטִיהֲרוּ אֶת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: They found a reason and declared the Land of Israel pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: עִילָּא מָצְאוּ וְטִיהֲרוּ אֶת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by reusing the principle from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים used the empty search as a reason to keep ארץ ישראל pure.

steps.title: New משנה: doubts about נגעים
steps.stepSummary: A doubt about נגעים is pure at the start, but once the person has been declared impure, a doubt is treated as impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Every doubt about נגעים is pure at the beginning, as long as the person has not yet been declared impure. Once he has been declared impure, his doubt is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a doubt about נגעים depends on whether the person has already been declared impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before any ruling of טומאה, we leave the person in his pure status when there is a doubt. Once he has been declared impure, the doubt stays impure, because we leave him in his current status.

keyTerms.meaning: a doubt about a צרעת mark

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the idea that a doubt keeps a person in the status he already has, which the גמרא will go on to explain.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Every doubt about leprous marks at the start is pure —
as long as he has not yet been declared impure.
Once he has been declared impure — his doubt is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל סְפֵק נְגָעִים בַּתְּחִילָּה, טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt about נגעים is pure before the person is declared impure and impure after.

steps.title: Where does the rule about doubtful נגעים come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a doubt in נגעים is pure at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins discussing the previous משנה. It asks for the source of the rule about doubtful נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a doubt about נגעים is treated as pure before the person was ever declared impure. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק or reason supports this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: 'These matters' means the rule just taught: a doubt in נגעים is pure at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule taught in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that a doubt in נגעים at the start is pure.

steps.title: The פסוק mentions purity first
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the פסוק says 'to declare him pure or to declare him impure', putting purity first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The פסוק says 'to declare him pure or to declare him impure.' Since the פסוק opened with purity first, a doubt is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a source. The פסוק about נגעים mentions 'pure' before 'impure.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since purity comes first in the פסוק, the תורה is showing that purity is the default in נגעים. So when we are unsure, we lean toward pure.

keyTerms.meaning: To declare him pure or to declare him impure

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The verse states: 'to pronounce it pure or to pronounce it impure.'
Since the verse opened [with it]
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it's part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: with purity first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order of the words in the פסוק, with purity first, shows that a doubt in נגעים is pure.

steps.title: Then every doubt should be pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if this is the source, then even after he was declared impure, a doubt should still be pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even after he was declared impure, his doubt should also be pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's source. That source proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not divide between before and after the person was declared impure. So if the פסוק makes doubts pure, it should make all doubts pure. But the משנה said that after he is declared impure, a doubt is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Once he has been declared impure

phrases.english: If so, even once he has been determined impure,
his uncertainty should also be pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's use of 'לטהרו או לטמאו' as the source for the rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's reason applies to all doubts, so it would contradict the משנה's rule that a doubt after impurity is impure.

steps.title: רב's teaching was really said about a different dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב's teaching was really said about the case of the בהרת and the white hair. There the תנא קמא says a doubt is impure and רבי יהושע says 'כיהה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the statement of רב יהודה in the name of רב was said about this: If the בהרת came before the white hair, he is impure. If the white hair came before the בהרת, he is pure. If it is unclear, he is impure. And רבי יהושע said: 'כיהה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls back. It says רב's teaching was never meant for our משנה, but for a different משנה about נגעים, which it now quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the quoted משנה, the doubt is about which sign came first. That is a doubt at the very start, before he was declared impure. רבי יהושע disagrees with the ruling of impure, and רב's פסוק will explain his view. So the פסוק does not need to cover doubts after impurity at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said about this (moving a teaching to another place)
A bright white spot, one sign of צרעת
White hair, another sign of צרעת
Literally 'dimmed'; the גמרא will explain it next

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. The תנא קמא here rules that a doubt is impure even at the start. It is רבי יהושע's view that fits the rule from step 9.

phrases.english: Rather, when it was stated,
that which Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
it was stated about this:

phrases.aramaic: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קָדְמָה לְשֵׂעָר לָבָן — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: If the baheret came before the white hair, he is impure;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שֵׂעָר לָבָן קוֹדֵם לַבַּהֶרֶת — טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: and if the white hair came before the baheret, he is pure.
If it is uncertain, he is impure.
phrases.notes: He is unsure which came first, the spot or the hair.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua said: Keiha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, אַהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by moving רב's teaching to a different משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocation: the teaching is moved to another context.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's פסוק was given as the source for our משנה's rule about doubtful נגעים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's פסוק was said to explain רבי יהושע's view about a doubt at the start, in the case of the בהרת and the white hair.

steps.title: What does 'כיהה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהושע meant by 'כיהה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'כיהה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the unclear word 'כיהה' means. It is setting up רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's one word does not tell us whether the person ends up pure or impure. The גמרא needs that cleared up.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'keiha'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבי יהושע's word in step 13 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע's 'כיהה' leads to pure or impure.

steps.title: It is unclear, and he is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains: the matter is unclear, and he is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is unclear, and he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that רבי יהושע ruled the case unclear, and so pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע disagrees with the תנא קמא who said impure. For him, when we cannot tell which sign came first, the person stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is unclear, and he is pure

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: It is unclear, and he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word's meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כיהה' means the case is unclear and he is pure.

steps.title: Maybe it means unclear and impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: perhaps 'כיהה' means it is unclear and he is impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it means: it is unclear, and he is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יהודה's reading. The word alone could just as well mean impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כיהה' only says the case is unclear. Nothing in the word itself decides whether the result is pure or impure, so רב יהודה needs a reason for choosing pure.

phrases.english: And perhaps it is unclear and he is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's explanation in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as easily mean 'unclear and impure', so the choice of pure needs support.

steps.title: The פסוק puts purity first, so the reading is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings רב's פסוק: since the תורה mentions purity first, an unclear case is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The פסוק says 'to declare him pure or to declare him impure.' Since the פסוק opened with purity first, he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה backs up his reading with רב's פסוק. This is where רב's teaching truly belongs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק from step 11 now explains רבי יהושע's view: in a doubt at the start, purity comes first. Here it causes no problem, because the doubt is before the person was ever declared impure.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's פסוק 'לטהרו או לטמאו' (purity first) is the source for רבי יהושע: a doubt in נגעים at the start is pure. It is not a rule that every doubt in נגעים is pure.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The verse states: 'to pronounce it pure or to pronounce it impure.'
Since the verse opened with it
with purity first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָמַר קְרָא ״לְטַהֲרוֹ אוֹ לְטַמְּאוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 with the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק puts purity first, 'כיהה' means unclear and pure.

steps.title: Seven ways to check a זב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that before declaring a person a זב, we check seven possible causes of the discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In seven ways we check a זב, as long as he has not yet been declared a זב: food, drink, carrying a load, jumping, sickness, a sight, and a thought.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists seven things we check to see whether something else caused the discharge, before he is declared a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the discharge came from an outside cause, like overeating or carrying something heavy, it does not count toward making him a זב. The checking only happens before he is declared a זב, much like the 'at the start' idea about נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a discharge that makes him impure

phrases.english: MISHNA: In seven ways
one examines the zav,
as long as he has not yet been determined to have ziva:
with regard to food and with regard to drink,
with regard to a burden and with regard to jumping,
and with regard to sickness, and with regard to a sight, and with regard to a thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the discussion of נגעים ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a person is declared a זב, we check seven possible outside causes of the discharge: food, drink, a load, jumping, sickness, a sight, and a thought.

steps.title: Once he is a confirmed זב, we stop checking
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that once someone is confirmed as a זב, we no longer check for outside causes. Even a discharge from an outside cause, a doubtful discharge, or semen makes him טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he is established as a זב, we do not check him anymore. A discharge caused by an outside factor, a doubtful discharge, and even his semen are all טמא, because there is good reason to assume it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the rule from Step 18. Checking for the seven causes only happens before a man becomes a confirmed זב; after that, we stop checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before he is a זב, we look for an innocent explanation, such as food or illness, before calling him טמא. Once he already has the status of a זב, his body has shown it produces זיבה. So any later discharge, even one with an outside cause or even semen, is treated as טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Became established as a זב (after two clear sightings)
His discharge caused by an outside factor (one of the seven causes)
His discharge that may or may not be זיבה
There is a basis for the matter; a good reason to assume it

phrases.english: Once he has been established as having zivah —
we do not examine him.
phrases.notes: This is the seven-cause check from Step 18.

phrases.english: His discharge from an outside cause, and his doubtful discharge,
and his semen — are all impure.
Because there is a basis for the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the checking rule from Step 18: it applies only before the man is confirmed as a זב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a man is confirmed as a זב, every later discharge is טמא without checking, because his established status is רגלים לדבר.

steps.title: The beaten victim who improved and then died
steps.stepSummary: Someone was beaten, was expected to die, improved, then worsened and died. The תנא קמא holds the attacker liable. רבי נחמיה exempts him, because the improvement is good reason to blame something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person strikes his friend and doctors estimate the victim will die, and then he gets better, but afterward gets worse and dies, the attacker is liable. רבי נחמיה says he is exempt, because there is good reason to think so.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another case that uses the idea of רגלים לדבר, this time from the laws of murder. There is a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא assumes the beating caused the death in the end, so the attacker is liable. רבי נחמיה says the victim's improvement points to a new cause of death. Here the phrase רגלים לדבר works in the attacker's favor and exempts him.

keyTerms.meaning: They estimated that he would die

steps.confusionAlert: The same phrase שרגלים לדבר appears in both cases but points in opposite directions. For the זב it makes him טמא. Here, for רבי נחמיה, it exempts the attacker.

phrases.english: One who strikes his fellow
and they estimated that he would die,
phrases.notes: They are the experts who judge how serious the injury is.

phrases.english: and he improved from what he had been,
afterward he worsened and died — he is liable.
Rabbi Nechemya says: he is exempt,
because there is a basis for the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case from a different area of law that uses the same reasoning, רגלים לדבר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds the attacker liable. רבי נחמיה exempts him because the victim's recovery suggests another cause of death.

steps.title: What is the source for the זב rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a זב is checked before he is confirmed but not after.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the תורה source of the rule in Step 19. It is setting up רבי נתן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the line between checking and not checking. Why do we check up to the confirmation of a זב, and stop at the third sighting?

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the זב rule from Step 19 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches we check a זב only before he is confirmed.

steps.title: רבי נתן learns it from ״והזב את זובו״
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן explains that the words ״הזב״ and ״זובו״ stand for two sightings. At the third sighting, the Torah compares the man to a woman, who is never checked for outside causes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: The פסוק says ״והזב את זובו״. For the third sighting, the man is compared to a female.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן answers the question with a פסוק. Its wording counts the first two sightings and then compares the third one to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״הזב״ and ״זובו״ count as two sightings, and those are checked. The פסוק continues ״לזכר ולנקבה״. For the third sighting, after he is already a זב, it puts the man next to a woman. A woman's discharge is טמא no matter what caused it, so his is too.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared (by placing the two side by side in a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said:
The verse says: "And the zav, his discharge,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:33. He counts ״הזב״ and ״זובו״ as the first two sightings.

phrases.english: for the third sighting
he is compared to a female.
phrases.notes: The same פסוק goes on to say ״לזכר ולנקבה״, for a male and a female, and a woman is never checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question from Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״הזב את זובו״ covers two sightings that are checked. The third sighting is compared to a woman, so it is not checked.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר still checks at the third sighting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן from a teaching of רבי אליעזר, who says we still check at the third sighting and stop only at the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, at the third sighting we check him; at the fourth we do not check him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks Step 22. רבי אליעזר seems to read the matter differently, so how does the פסוק fit his view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן's reading makes the third sighting the point where checking stops. רבי אליעזר moves that point to the fourth sighting. So where in the פסוק does he find a third sighting that still gets checked?

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says
at the third we examine him,
at the fourth we do not examine him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי נתן's derivation in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן's reading that the פסוק stops checking at the third sighting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר checks the third sighting too. That does not fit a פסוק that only counts two checked sightings.

steps.title: They disagree about whether the word את teaches something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר learns from every את, so ״הזב את זובו״ counts three sightings. The רבנן do not learn from את, so they count only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about the word ״את״. רבי אליעזר learns from ״את״, and the רבנן do not learn from ״את״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Both sides read the same פסוק, but they disagree about whether the small word את counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, ״הזב״, ״את״, and ״זובו״ make three sightings that are checked, so checking stops at the fourth. For the רבנן, the word את is just grammar. Only two sightings are counted, so checking stops at the third. רבי נתן follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns a teaching from the word

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees we check a זב before he is confirmed and stop after. The only argument is whether ״הזב את זובו״ counts two sightings (the רבנן) or three (רבי אליעזר, who learns from את).

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about the word "et":
Rabbi Eliezer expounds the word "et."
phrases.notes: So he counts ״הזב״, ״את״, and ״זובו״ as three sightings.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis do not expound the word "et."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23 by explaining how רבי אליעזר reads the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the disagreement in a basic rule of reading the Torah: whether the word את teaches something.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי אליעזר's view does not fit the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר counts את as a third sighting, while the רבנן (and רבי נתן) count only two.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: his forced and doubtful discharges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words אונסו וספיקו to begin discussing that part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: his discharge caused by outside factors, and his doubtful discharge, are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a short phrase from the משנה to open a new discussion. This is a setup line that prepares for what the גמרא will say about these words next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that after a man is confirmed as a זב, even an אונס discharge (caused by eating, illness, and the like) or a ספק discharge (one we are unsure about) still makes him impure. This matches the earlier steps: before he is confirmed, we check for outside causes, and after that, we stop checking. The גמרא now turns to this specific ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: His discharge caused by an outside factor, such as food, illness, or strain, and not by a real זיבה
His discharge that we are unsure about, where it is not clear whether it counts as זיבה

phrases.english: His discharge caused by outside factors, and his doubtful discharge.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. The משנה says these discharges are impure once he is already a confirmed זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how many sightings come before we stop checking a זב (steps 21-24), the גמרא now quotes the משנה's ruling about what happens once he is confirmed: an אונס or ספק discharge still makes him impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a man is a confirmed זב, his discharge caused by outside factors and his doubtful discharge are both treated as impure.
